title: Console rollup pruning and staged acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Reduce surface area for Console observability to a minimal, verifiable rollup that supports launch SLAs: one consolidated dashboards tile, a lightweight trace picker, and a single route-level cost rollup. Define staged acceptance so engineering can cut further if needed.
background: PMs and Eng aligned on trimming Console telemetry for initial launch after capacity and cost concerns. Several prior tickets scoped larger surface area; this ticket captures a pragmatic pruning that preserves critical use cases (incident triage, per-route cost visibility) while minimizing backend ingestion and UI complexity.
problem_statement: Current Console plan contains multiple dashboard cards, detailed span-level trace listing, and per-token cost breakdowns that exceed launch budget and implementation velocity. We need a defensible minimum set of features and concrete acceptance criteria so devs can implement a tight slice and ship with confidence.
proposed_solution: Deliver a 'rollup' telemetry surface: (1) a single consolidated Dashboard tile that shows request volume, p50/p95 latency, and error rate for selected routes; (2) a trace-picker that returns representative traces (one per route with metadata) rather than full trace timelines; (3) a route-level cost rollup that shows aggregated cost and request-weighted average latency. Implement UI toggles to enable expanded views later. Staged acceptance: alpha (backend + smoke UI), beta (full route selection + basic filters), launch (SLOs and alerting hooks).
tradeoffs: Reduces visibility into per-span timing — may slow root-cause in complex incidents
Aggregated cost hides token-level anomalies — some billing investigations will need offline tooling
Simpler UI may not satisfy power users; mitigate with explicit roadmap for expanded views
acceptance_criteria: Alpha: Dashboard tile deployed to Console staging showing request count, p50, p95, error rate for a selected route; data refresh <= 30s; smoke tests pass
Alpha: Trace-picker endpoint returns up to 5 representative traces per route with metadata (trace id, duration, status, sample reason); UI displays list of trace summaries without full flamegraphs
Alpha: Route cost rollup endpoint returns total cost and requests per route for last 24h and last 7d; UI displays percent change compared to previous period
Beta: Filters by route and time-range in UI function correctly; no more than 2 extra backend queries per user action
Launch: Backend ingestion increases <= 25% relative to current baseline forecast; storage cost impact validated with finance
Launch: End-to-end latency from request arrival to dashboard visibility <= 2 minutes for 90% of requests in staging
Launch: Alerts fire for missing telemetry (no data for a route) and for error-rate SLO breaches; on-call runbook updated
out_of_scope: Per-token cost breakdowns (deferred to post-launch billing diagnostics)
Full span timeline UI and flamegraph visualization
High-cardinality metrics / user-level drilldowns in v1

risks: Under-indexing traces may miss rare high-impact failures
If backend query count per action is too high, Console performance may suffer under load
Finance may deny additional capacity trailing launch if usage grows faster than forecast
rollout_plan: Canary to 5% of orgs for 48 hours, monitor ingestion and UI latency. If errors or ingestion spike > 30% of forecast, rollback to feature flag off for rollout cohort. Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with monitoring gates at each step.
metrics: Track: ingestion rate, storage delta, dashboard query latency, UI error rate, alert firing rate, number of times per-token billing investigation is required (as a tradeoff KPI)
